newsitem.title: CHINA: China says makes gains in plan to end leaded petrol.
newsitem.headline: China says makes gains in plan to end leaded petrol.

text.p: China has already made gains in its plan to step up output of unleaded gasoline to replace leaded fuel by the year 2000, an official from the China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) said on Tuesday.

The output of unleaded gasoline has been increasing annually and 51.6 percent of the gasoline produced by state oil refiner Sinopec was unleaded in 1996, said Jiang Lu, deputy director of Sinopec's production and management division.
China produced 30.53 million tonnes of gasoline in 1996 while the output of Sinopec alone was 24.26 million tonnes, he said.
"More than half of the (gasoline producing) enterprises have stopped producing leaded gasoline," Jiang said in a speech at an industry conference.
He gave no figure for the total number of enterprises producing gasoline.
The average content of lead in gasoline used on the domestic market was 0.028 grams per litre and the average content of lead in leaded gasoline was 0.049 grams per litre, Jiang said.
China has also been trying to shift to high octane gasoline but there is still demand for low octane fuel, he said.
